inventive_nucleus: A bioresorbable polymer locking mechanism is integrated into a self-expanding nitinol mesh to prevent septal occluder device embolization.
mechanism: The locking mechanism interacts with the septal surface to prevent displacement of the nitinol mesh.
causal_chain: The locking mechanism detects these changes
The locking mechanism triggers the geometric locking mechanism
The geometric locking mechanism locks the nitinol mesh
The locking mechanism monitors its own degradation
The locking mechanism degrades after 6 months
expected_effect: The device prevents septal occluder device embolization by locking the nitinol mesh in place.

predictions.conditions: In a cohort of 100 patients with a mean follow-up of 6 months, using the Nucleus device in conjunction with standard septal occluder device placement procedures
predictions.falsifier: A study showing that the Nucleus device does not significantly reduce septal occluder device embolization rates in a cohort of 100 patients with a mean follow-up of 6 months, or a study demonstrating that the Nucleus device is associated with a higher rate of complications compared to the current standard of care.

falsification_tests: A study showing that the Nucleus device does not significantly reduce septal occluder device embolization rates in a cohort of 100 patients with a mean follow-up of 6 months, or a study demonstrating that the Nucleus device is associated with a higher rate of complications compared to the current standard of care.

experiment_plan.objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of a bioresorbable polymer locking mechanism integrated into a self-expanding nitinol mesh to prevent septal occluder device embolization.
independent_variables: Presence of bioresorbable polymer locking mechanism
controls: Standard septal occluder device placement procedures without the locking mechanism
experiment_plan.baseline: Current Rate of 5% septal occluder device embolization
procedure: Recruit 100 patients with a mean follow-up of 6 months
Randomly assign patients to either the Nucleus device group or the control group
Place the septal occluder device in both groups using standard procedures
Monitor patients for 6 months to assess embolization rates
experiment_plan.expected_result: A decrease in septal occluder device embolization rate by at least 70%
experiment_plan.falsification_condition: A study showing that the Nucleus device does not significantly reduce septal occluder device embolization rates, or a study demonstrating that the Nucleus device is associated with a higher rate of complications compared to the current standard of care
experiment_plan.sample_requirements: 100 patients with a mean follow-up of 6 months
experiment_plan.safety_constraints: Ensure that the Nucleus device does not cause any adverse effects or complications in patients
experiment_plan.information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of the bioresorbable polymer locking mechanism in preventing septal occluder device embolization and its potential impact on patient outcomes

commercial.economic_problem: Reduced risk of device embolization and associated medical costs
commercial.manufacturing_relevance: High, as the device requires precise manufacturing of nitinol mesh and bioresorbable polymer components
commercial.regulatory_path_hypothesis: Class III, as it involves a medical device that interacts with the body and requires FDA clearance
commercial.commercial_reason: High commercial potential due to the significant economic problem it solves and the high demand for septal occluder devices in the medical industry
